items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-05-10
items.q: You know, the one Piku played

ctx.x: That's what I'm talking about. Yeah, some kind of stuff to fix up. Moe's Chelsea in Shreeport. Man, the Patterson, we caught up with him, you know, we know he's smoking something. So we had a job down in Mansfield, you see. We all had to get room to sleep that night. So Moe's got him a room by himself, you know, and he had a whole suitcase with him besides his Violet case, you know. Man, he said, we gonna have some fun tonight when we get off from that dam. items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-01-16
items.q: Piku was on that job. He was playing the alto strikes and playing there.

ctx.x: Would it be 1900 or would it be 1910 or 1920 or what?

No, I don't think it was that far back. That's it. Dewey used to wait on Basin Street, Emmanuel Perez. That's when I was very small. Yeah, that must bring back. Let's see, wait, I got to get that thing straight. I think Tom could tell you better than I could about that. Tom Alba? Yeah. Because I had learned how to play cornet, you know, and Tom was playing the violin. And Eddie Vincent was practicing every day with us. And then all at once he picked up and he left there with Jimmy Fallon and then we went north.…
